subject: Request: Chief approval for contract risk & terms amendments - Edge Health
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@edgehealth.com>

Cc: contracts@edgehealth.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Edge Health SOW v3 - redlines attached

Hi Laura,

Thanks for getting the draft over. Our procurement team reviewed and attached a redlined SOW (EdgeHealth_SOW_v3_redlines.pdf). The main changes are summarized below: 

- Removal of limitation of liability and a request for unlimited liability in certain data-related incidents.
- Broader indemnity language that would require Redwood to indemnify Edge Health for third-party claims related to PHI/PII exposures, even where our integration partners are involved.
- Warranty period extended to 24 months with specific performance SLAs and remedy obligations.
- Requests for additional audit rights and a retention clause that would require longer storage of logs.

We are on a tight timeline — procurement would like confirmation of acceptance of these redlines by end of day Monday so we can proceed with finance. If there are items you need to escalate, please let me know whom we should expect a final answer from.

Attaching the redlines for your legal team.

Regards,
Tom Ellis
VP, Procurement
Edge Health

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Chief approval for contract risk & terms amendments - Edge Health

Team — forwarding procurement redlines from Edge Health. Key commercial impact and legal asks summarized below (see attached redlines_summary.xlsx for a line-by-line):

Summary of high-risk items:
- Indemnity: they want broad indemnity including third-party claims tied to PHI/PII; language reads as an open-ended obligation.
- Liability cap: their markup removes the limitation of liability in consequence of "data incidents" — effectively unlimited exposure.
- Warranty: 24-month warranty and SLA remedies that could trigger priced credits and extended liability windows.
- Audit/retention: long retention and audit rights that could increase hosting and compliance costs.

Our current posture and recommended responses:
- Do NOT accept unlimited liability. Recommend a negotiated liability cap at $2,000,000 OR 12 months of net fees (whichever is lower). If Edge insists above that, escalate to CEO level.
- Indemnity: limit to claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; include carve-outs for downstream partner responsibilities. For data-related claims, propose a separate DPA and cyber-liability carve.
- Warranty: reduce to 90 days for defect claims; tie SLA credits to clear availability thresholds.
- Concessions we can offer without changing risk profile materially: 15% first-year credit, two months of professional services (onboarding), and a prioritized support SLA for the first 6 months.

Commercial impact: acceptance of their redlines as-is would expose us to multi-million dollar unbounded risk and would require underwriting approval. The deal size (annual committed spend) is projected at $600k ARR.

Action requested: need Chief-level approval to either (A) push back with the positions above and offer the stated concessions, or (B) approve escalation to CEO/CRO for an exception to increase cap/indemnity (I recommend A). Please provide an explicit sign-off by EOD Mon (11/30) so I can respond to their procurement deadline.

Attachments: redlines_summary.xlsx, EdgeHealth_SOW_v3_redlines.pdf

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cell: (415) 555-0189

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 13:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Chief approval for contract risk & terms amendments - Edge Health

Laura — reviewed the redline PDF and your summary. High-level legal notes and suggested text: 

1) Limitation of Liability
- We should not accept language that removes the cap. Proposed clause: "Except for liability resulting from each party's willful misconduct or gross negligence or liability for indemnification obligations for IP infringement, each party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (i) $2,000,000 or (ii) twelve (12) months of fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order."
- If procurement pushes back, we can offer a phased escalation: CEO sign-off required for any cap increase above $2M; CRO to approve up to $3M with documented risk acceptance.

2) Indemnity
- Narrow indemnity to (a) IP infringement claims, (b) claims arising solely from Redwood's material breach or gross negligence.
- For data/PHI claims, propose a separate cyber-liability carve that limits to proven Redwood breach and aligns with our cyber insurance. Offer to include an express DPA with standard breach notification timelines.

3) Warranty
- Counter to 90 days and limit remedies to repair/replacement or pro-rated service credits tied to explicit uptime metrics. 

4) Audit/Retention
- Push back on unlimited log retention and broad audit rights. Allow one annual audit, with scope limited to Redwood-controlled systems and with cost-sharing if more than one audit per year is requested.

Recommended next steps:
- Send a firm pushback to procurement with the above alternatives and the attached redline (I will produce redline language this afternoon).
- If Edge Health insists on unlimited cap or broad indemnity, route to CEO for a decision.

If you want, I'll draft a short escalation memo for the CEO that explains exposure and the business rationale for either accepting a higher cap or walking.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Legal, Contracts | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Chief approval for contract risk & terms amendments - Edge Health

Thanks Laura and Aditya — good, pragmatic analysis. I support the recommended position: stand firm on a $2M / 12 months fees cap, narrow indemnity per Aditya's language, and 90-day warranty. Offer 15% credit + two months PS as commercial sweetener. 

Requesting final sign-off from CEO (cc'd on escalation when we send). If CEO/COO prefer to move faster, we can offer a one-time exception up to $3M with contingency that Edge purchases a cyber-liability endorsement or provides additional security assurances (SOC 2 + annual pen test report).

Laura — please prepare a short executive escalation note (1 page) summarizing exposure, financial tradeoffs, and recommended fallback, and mark for CEO decision if they push for unlimited language. I'll approve escalation to the CEO if needed.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
